LVGLab 0.15.0 lets an application change theme colors at runtime, for example a color the user picks in a
companion app.

## Downloads

| Platform | File |
|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64), installer | `LVGLab-0.15.0-windows-x64-setup.exe` |
| Windows 10/11 (x64), portable | `LVGLab-0.15.0-windows-x64.zip` |
| Linux (x64, glibc 2.35+) | `LVGLab-0.15.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `LVGLab-0.15.0-macos-arm64.tar.gz` |
| macOS (Intel) | `LVGLab-0.15.0-macos-x64.tar.gz` |

The Windows installer adds a Start menu entry and can associate `.lvglab` files. The archives need no
installation: unpack and start `lvglab` (`lvglab.exe` on Windows). Check downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
On macOS, run `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine lvglab` once if the unsigned binary is refused.

## New

- **Runtime theme colors**: each color in the *Themes* panel has a *Runtime* checkbox. A runtime color is exported
  without `const` in `ui_themes.c/h`, so the application can write a new value into the color array and apply it
  with `ui_theme_set()`. Colors without the checkbox stay constant (in flash), as before.

## Note

- Projects that use runtime colors keep the setting only in LVGLab 0.15.0 or newer. Saving such a project in an
  older version drops the checkbox, and the next export makes the colors `const` again.
